decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with through-glass vias sit at the core of Plan Optik's announced advanced-packaging and MEMS direction, so management will keep investing and treat weak results as temporary.
Carrier wafers are a low-cost extension of the established wafer business, publicly announced and easy to sustain, so there is little reason to withdraw them.

The Cu-interposer was launched with visible commitment at SEMICON Europa and has its own page, which raises the pressure to justify continued investment and to blame slow uptake on pandemic-era market conditions.
Wafer Universe was founded as a dedicated brand, a public commitment management would rather persist with than abandon, and off-the-shelf sales are cheap to maintain.

Glass-based circuit boards were only mentioned on the website and are less central to the firm's direction, but they fit the glass-substrate packaging strategy, so management likely keeps them while attributing slow demand to temporary causes.
